headline: Fable 5.2 takes the top spot, time to upgrade your Claude Code
summary: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 tops the model leaderboard; Gemini reportedly sends Drive files to human reviewers.

items.title: Fable 5.2 tops the chart, even better at coding
items.pitch: Anthropic dropped Fable 5.2 last night and it shot to #1 on the model leaderboard. The Claude Code you use every day can run it right now, and it's noticeably better at writing code.
why: #1 on Artificial Analysis, and the price dropped 20%
Simon Willison tested it: 3D modeling and tracking down weird noises both work
Available on all paid plans today, and existing users even get a usage reset
actions: Switch your model to claude-fable-5.2 in Claude Code and try it for a day
Try this prompt: tell it straight up that 'this codebase is yours' and it'll go refactor and dedupe on its own
deep_dive: Compared to the Opus 5.5 you're using, Fable 5.2 is better at long-running, multi-threaded hard work. Rauch says that much parallelism needs a cloud sandbox to handle it.
Getting started is basically free: you can pick it right in the Claude app and Claude Code. Heads up, the max thinking setting will burn through tokens without output, xhigh is steadier.
items.signals: HN 662 points · 842 comments · #1 on Artificial Analysis · Simon Willison tested it · $8/$40 per million tokens

items.title: Gemini sends Drive files to human review
items.pitch: A developer dug up that Gemini will hand your personal Drive files and emails to humans to review. If your company uses Google Workspace, be careful with payroll data.
why: There's a repo on GitHub with the evidence, HN 633 points
Sensitive files like payroll and performance reviews could be seen by third parties
Worth checking the data terms before your company uses Gemini
actions: Ask your company IT/security one question: will Gemini data be reviewed by humans
Keep sensitive payroll files out of Drive folders that auto-sync
deep_dive: This isn't a bug, it's Google's data handling being exposed. For your comp work at a multinational, it's a compliance point worth flagging in advance.
Whether it's real and how wide it goes depends on your company's contract terms, don't just trust a post; but asking a question doesn't hurt.
items.signals: HN 633 points · 134 comments · evidence in a GitHub repo

items.title: Meta ships Muse Ember, a cheap small model
items.pitch: Meta put out a small, fast model called Muse Ember, priced in the same tier as GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku, built for the repetitive grunt work inside agents.
why: The cheapest in the budget tier, Simon says it's on the value frontier
Good for repeated work like tool calls, extraction, and long doc parsing
items.signals: HN 310 points · Simon Willison tested it · $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens
